User is planning a flexible round-trip Economy trip from Washington, DC (DCA/IAD) to San Francisco, likely SFO, in a few weeks. Budget is about $400 round trip but willing to splurge for nonstop convenience. They recently said they reached United MileagePlus Premier Gold status (override the earlier note that said Premier Silver; status qualification should still be verified in their account). Nonstop IAD–SFO fares previously quoted at roughly $410–$430, but these and any claims about current sales/error fares were not live-verified. User prefers to wait for a price drop and wants to set fare alerts; assistant cannot create alerts directly. Suggested United fare alerts plus Google Flights/Skyscanner price tracking.

For an IAD–SFO round trip, the prior mileage estimate was about 2,465 miles per one-way segment. A Premier Gold member may earn a 50% MileagePlus bonus on qualifying flights, but the exact amount depends on fare class, route, exclusions, and round-trip itinerary. Earlier calculations treated one segment as a round trip and produced 3,697.5 total miles; this was misleading. Each eligible round-trip segment can earn based on distance/fare, with status bonuses applying when eligible. Premier Platinum qualification generally requires 75,000 Premier Qualifying Miles or 90 Premier Qualifying Segments in a calendar year, but current United requirements should be verified.

User asked about error fares/sales and how to track travel expenses. They currently use a spreadsheet and chose to try Expensify. Advice: start with Expensify’s free plan for personal use, then upgrade only if advanced automation, card/bank reconciliation, detailed reporting, or team/approval features become necessary. Verify current pricing/features; the earlier claim that a premium plan starts at $5/user/month billed annually and that a free trial is always available may be outdated or inaccurate.

Earlier award-travel context: User has Chase Ultimate Rewards points and may transfer them to United. Chase→MileagePlus transfers are generally 1:1 in 1,000-point increments and usually fast but irreversible. United award prices, inventory, and fees are dynamic; United’s checkout is authoritative. Premier status does not guarantee extra award inventory.

- User was told to log into Chase, open Ultimate Rewards/“Use points,” choose “Transfer to travel partners,” select United, provide the MileagePlus number and last name, enter the amount, and confirm. They should verify the linked account details carefully because transfers are generally irreversible.
- United award pricing, fees, and availability are dynamic. Earlier assistant estimates of 12,500 Saver, 20,000 Standard, and 30,000 Flex miles for DC–LAX may be outdated or inaccurate; the exact live award price should be checked in United’s booking flow. Premier Silver does not automatically guarantee extra award inventory.
- Award tickets require payment of applicable carrier-imposed and government taxes/fees. The prior rough estimate of $19.50 is not reliable; exact fees can depend on itinerary, departure airport, and carrier, and the checkout page is authoritative. The earlier claim of a universal $75 close-in award-booking fee is questionable; the $5.60 21-day ticketing fee generally applies to many itineraries, but verify current rules.

User’s immediate question: help estimate taxes and fees for a one-way United economy award from DC to LAX. Give a useful dollar range only with clear caveats and advise them to enter the desired itinerary/log in to United to see the exact total before confirming. Mention that the booking screen distinguishes taxes/fees and any ticketing charge.
